cards.explanation: The answer is that you do not know what a day may bring. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, says, "Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring." (Proverbs 27:1) I've announced a perfect batch before the dough was even mixed, and the oven made a liar out of me. Tomorrow is a batch nobody has peeked at yet, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, "Let another praise you, and not your own mouth…" and then adds that a stranger can do it too. (Proverbs 27:2) Praise lands better when somebody else hands it over. Clapping for yourself in an empty bakery just sounds like a single oven mitt flapping.

The answer is fool. The verse says a stone is heavy and sand is a burden, but "…aggravation from a fool outweighs them both." (Proverbs 27:3) That's some serious weight, friends. I've hauled a full cookie sheet across a bakery with one mustache, and even that felt lighter.

The answer is jealousy. Solomon says wrath is cruel and anger is like a flood, "…but who can withstand jealousy?" (Proverbs 27:4) He puts jealousy above the other two. That question hangs in the air, and I think nobody in the bakery wants to answer it.

The answer is deceitful. The verse says, "The wounds of a friend are faithful, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful." (Proverbs 27:6) A friend might sting you with the truth, but you can trust it. If my friend tells me my hat is crooked, I'd rather hear it before the customers do.

The answer is the soul that is full. The verse says, "The soul that is full loathes honey…" (Proverbs 27:7) When you're stuffed, even something sweet turns you off, friends. I've seen a baker push away a cookie after the fortieth sample, and I respected it.

The answer is True. The verse says, "…but to a hungry soul, any bitter thing is sweet." (Proverbs 27:7) When you're hungry enough, even bitter things taste good. Hunger changes what counts as a treat, friends.

The answer is a bird that strays from its nest. The verse says, "Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who wanders from his home." (Proverbs 27:8) A nest is where a bird belongs, and the verse puts a man's home in that same place. I know a little about being far from a warm spot, and I'd rather be near mine.

The answer is friend. The verse says, "Oil and incense bring joy to the heart, and the counsel of a friend is sweetness to the soul." (Proverbs 27:9) Good advice from a friend is as welcome as a warm oven on a cold morning. Hearing it from somebody who cares makes it go down easy.

The answer is True. The verse says, "better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away." (Proverbs 27:10) Solomon puts the one nearby ahead of the one far away. I'd say that's a good reason to be kind to whoever lives next door, friends.

The answer is that the speaker can answer the one who taunts him. He says, "Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, so that I can answer him who taunts me." (Proverbs 27:11) A wise son gives him something to say back. I think there's a proud dad in there somewhere.

The answer is False. The verse says, "The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty." (Proverbs 27:12) The prudent are the ones who see danger and take cover. The simple keep going and pay. I've smelled smoke from an oven and gone to open a window, and I recommend it, friends.

The answer is his garment. The verse says, "Take the garment of him who posts security for a stranger…" (Proverbs 27:13) That's Solomon's advice about a man who has posted security for a stranger. The verse names a garment, nothing fancier. Nice and plain, like a good cookie recipe.

The answer is curse. The verse says, "If one blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be counted to him as a curse." (Proverbs 27:14) Early and loud turns a blessing sour. Some blessings come better at a reasonable hour with the volume down, friends.

The answer is holding back the wind. The verse says restraining her is "…like holding back the wind or grasping oil with one’s right hand." (Proverbs 27:16) Both are things you can't really get a grip on. I've tried to catch wind in my apron, and all I got was a flappy apron.

The answer is sharpens. The verse says, "As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another." (Proverbs 27:17) Iron does the sharpening to iron, and one man does it to another. I spent years soft around the edges, so I know who I'd like next to me, friends.

The answers are master and honored. The verse says, "Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who looks after his master will be honored." (Proverbs 27:18) Tend the tree and you eat its fruit. Look after your master and you're honored. Care leads to a reward in both halves, friends.

The answer is the heart. The verse says, "As water reflects the face, so the heart reflects the true man." (Proverbs 27:19) Look into still water and you see your face. Look at the heart and you see the true man.

The answer is True. The verse says, "Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; so the eyes of man are never satisfied." (Proverbs 27:20) The eyes keep wanting more, just like those two. I've been guilty of eyeing one more cookie, and then another.

The answer is the praise accorded him. The verse says, "A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but a man is tested by the praise accorded him." (Proverbs 27:21) Fire tests metal, and praise tests a man. Being cheered can be tougher than it sounds, friends.

The answer is that it will not depart from him. The verse says, "Though you grind a fool like grain with mortar and a pestle, yet his folly will not depart from him." (Proverbs 27:22) Even grinding him like grain doesn't remove it. Some things don't come out no matter how hard you press.

The answer is that riches are not forever. The verse says, "…for riches are not forever, nor does a crown endure to every generation." (Proverbs 27:24) What you have now won't last by itself. So you pay attention to it, the way I check the oven timer, friends.

The answer is clothing. The verse says, "…the lambs will provide you with clothing, and the goats with the price of a field." (Proverbs 27:26) Lambs cover your back, and goats can buy you a field. Looking after the flock has real payoffs, friends.

The answer is False. The verse says there will be plenty of goats' milk to feed you, with "…food for your household and nourishment for your maidservants." (Proverbs 27:27) So the milk is for you and the household, not just you. There's enough to go around, friends.
